commonFaq.q: Is anything on this site a booking?
commonFaq.a: No. Carnival Ride Rental shows ride inventory from independent operators and, through Event Access, gives you their direct contact details. The rental itself, including availability, price, contract and payment, is agreed directly between you and the operator.

commonFaq.q: Who sets up and runs the ride?
commonFaq.a: The operator who owns it. Operators deliver, set up and run their rides with their own crews. Confirm staffing, hours and setup time with each operator you talk to.

commonFaq.q: How much space and power does a ride need?
commonFaq.a: It depends on the ride and the operator's equipment. Have your surface, available space, access route and power details ready, and ask each operator what their ride needs before you commit.

Some cities, counties and venues require permits or approvals for amusement rides. Requirements vary by location, so check with your venue and local authority and ask the operator what they usually need from a site.

groups.name: Birthdays
planningNotes: Have the guests' ages ready so operators can suggest rides that suit them.
Backyards often have limited access for trucks and trailers. Note gates, slopes and overhead wires before you call.
Weekend dates in peak season go early; start contacting operators well ahead.

groups.name: Religious & cultural celebrations
planningNotes: Know the schedule of the day (ceremony, meal, dancing) so the ride runs when guests are free to use it.
Venues such as banquet halls and places of worship may have rules about outdoor equipment; check before you contact operators.
Tell operators the guests' age mix; many of these events include young children and grandparents.

groups.name: Family milestones & parties
planningNotes: Describe the site to operators: lawn, driveway, parking lot or venue grounds.
Have the expected number of guests and their ages ready.
If the venue is rented, ask the venue manager about ride rules before you call operators.

groups.name: Schools & youth groups
planningNotes: Schools and districts often require paperwork from vendors; ask your administration what they need and tell operators early.
Have the grades or ages attending and the expected head count ready.
Note where trucks can reach the field or lot.

groups.name: Colleges & universities
planningNotes: Campus events often go through student activities and risk management; start that approval early.
Have the expected attendance and operating hours ready.
Note where trucks can load in and the surface the ride would stand on.

groups.name: Corporate events
planningNotes: Say whether employees' families are invited, so operators can suggest rides for a range of ages.
Company venues and rented grounds may need vendor documentation; ask your facilities or events team.
Have your operating hours and expected attendance ready.

groups.name: Community & civic events
planningNotes: Public events usually need city or county approval; check with the organiser or permitting office early.
Have the expected attendance and the number of event days ready.
Describe the site to operators: street, park, fairground or parking lot.

groups.name: Holidays & seasonal events
planningNotes: Holiday dates are in high demand; contact operators as early as you can.
Say whether the event is a single day or runs over several days.
Weather can affect ride operation; ask each operator about their weather policy before you sign.

groups.name: Fundraisers
planningNotes: Decide how you plan to run the rides (wristbands, tickets or free) so operators can quote accordingly.
Have the expected attendance and event hours ready.
Know who is responsible for the site and any approvals.

groups.name: Venues & properties
planningNotes: Property managers and landlords may need vendor paperwork; check before you contact operators.
Describe the surface, space and access where the ride would go.
Have the expected number of residents, customers or guests ready.
